deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Gauss's second method (Math.12, folios 27r–27v) for evaluating the 'Decident'. The Decident appears to be the integer that fixes the biquadratic character of one Gaussian prime with respect to another, i.e. the exponent k in [m/M] = i^k (my reading). The previous page wrote it as a sum of five parts I–V plus a correction q. Each part is a sum Σ of signs ε = ±1 over lattice points, with side conditions such as 'X ganz' (X an integer) or '[X] gerade' (the integer part of X is even). Some parts carry a weight λ, the 'Intensor' of a residue p. The Intensor is the exponent k in 0..3 attached to a unit or residue class i^k.

This page rewrites parts II and IV and then merges pieces of them.

(A) Part II. On the previous page, part II was Σ λ ε, with λ = Int(p). Gauss now replaces λ by λ' = Int(ip). Since multiplying by i raises the exponent by 1, λ' = λ+1 mod 4, so λ = λ' − 1 + 4·[λ' = 0] = λ' − 1 + 4·[λ = 3] (step made explicit by me). Hence Σλε = Σλ'ε − Σε + 4Σ_{λ=3} ε.
- On the page this reads: −Σε over 'Y ganz, [X] gerade', plus 4Σε over those points that also have '[x] gerade, [y] ungerade'.
- So the condition λ = 3 corresponds to ([x] even, [y] odd). This is consistent with the Intensor being read off from the parities of the integer parts of the coordinates.
- The term +Σλ'ε is then paired with the old part III, −Σλ'ε over 'X ganz, [Y] ungerade'.
- Gauss states that these two weighted sums merge into a new III: +Σε over [X] even, [Y] odd; −4Σε over points where x is an integer and [y] is odd; plus boundary corrections r + s.
- r = 0 when the sign pair of (A,B) is ++, −+ or −−, and r = Int(ω m i) when it is +−.
- s = (−?)Int((½−ω) m i) when (M−1)/2 is even and B > 0, and s = 0 otherwise.
- The merge itself is presumably a lattice-point/boundary argument; it is not carried out on the page.
- In the running example, III is empty and r = s = 0.

(B) Part IV. Here λ' = Int(im − ip). The table on the previous page gives λ' = 0, 3, 2, 1 for λ = 0, 1, 2, 3, i.e. λ' ≡ −λ mod 4. Thus λ = −λ' + 4·[λ ≠ 0], so Σλε = −Σλ'ε + 4Σ_{λ≠0} ε.
- On the page: +4Σε over 'Y ganz, [X] gerade', excluding points that are simultaneously '[x] gerade, [y] gerade'. So λ = 0 corresponds to ([x] even, [y] even).
- This leaves −Σλ'ε over 'Y ganz, [X] gerade', to be combined with old part V, +Σλ'ε over 'X ganz, [Y] gerade'.
- These merge into V: +Σε over points where [X] and [Y] are not both even; −4Σε over points where x is an integer and [y] is even; plus w.
- w = 0 when (M−1)/2 is even and A > 0. In all other cases w = −Intensor((½ i + ω) m).
- The next page evaluates V for the example and tabulates q, r, s, w and their sums for all sign and parity cases.

Purpose: this is a Gauss-lemma / lattice-point evaluation of the biquadratic residue symbol, aimed at biquadratic reciprocity.
errors: No outright error is visible. The merging steps (II+III → III, IV+V → V, with the corrections r, s, w) are asserted without derivation, so they cannot be checked from this page alone.
In III Gauss corrected the condition '[x] Gerade' to 'x eine Ganze, [y] Ungerade' (with x/X overwritten). In IV he struck out 'positiv' and wrote 'gerade'. These are self-corrections, not errors.

Possible sign issue: as transcribed, s = Int((½−ω)mi), but the tabulated s values on the next page are negative (−2, −3). This suggests the page actually reads s = −Int(...), and the image shows a stroke before 'Int'.
The example gives w = 2 on the next page, while the next page's table lists w only as negative entries. This may be a matter of the residue convention mod 4; it cannot be resolved from this page.

results.what: Converting Intensor-weighted sums: Int(ip) = Int(p)+1 mod 4, giving Σλε = Σλ'ε − Σε + 4Σ_{λ=3}ε. Similarly Int(i(m−p)) ≡ −Int(p), giving Σλε = −Σλ'ε + 4Σ_{λ≠0}ε. Combined with the parity description of λ through [x], [y].
results.modern_name: Bookkeeping of the biquadratic Gauss-lemma exponent (the index of the unit i^k)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss lemma analogues for quartic residues: Gauss (Nachlass); published forms by Eisenstein and later authors

results.what: Reduction of the 'Decident' (exponent of the biquadratic character) to counts of lattice points with parity conditions, plus explicit boundary corrections r, s, w depending on the signs of A, B and the parity of (M−1)/2
results.modern_name: Lattice-point (Eisenstein-style) proof strategy for biquadratic reciprocity in Z[i]
results.usually_credited_to: Biquadratic reciprocity is stated by Gauss (1832). First published proofs are Jacobi (lectures 1836/37) and Eisenstein (1844); lattice-point style proofs are associated with Eisenstein.

deep.surprise_reason: It is known from the Werke (Nachlass) and from secondary literature that Gauss had unpublished material, including the 'Decident' formulation, towards a proof of biquadratic reciprocity. This page is a detailed technical step in that programme, with explicit boundary corrections. It is notable as an unpublished detail but not a new attribution.

checkable.sympy: all(Mod(l+1,4) == l+1-4*(1 if l==3 else 0) for l in range(4))
checkable.asserts: Int(ip) = Int(p)+1 mod 4 equals λ+1−4[λ=3], which underlies the rewritten part II (−Σε + 4Σ_{λ=3}ε + Σλ'ε).

checkable.sympy: all(l == Mod(l+1,4) - 1 + 4*(1 if l==3 else 0) for l in range(4))
checkable.asserts: λ = λ' − 1 + 4[λ=3], the decomposition used for part II.
Int(im−ip) ≡ −Int(p) mod 4 gives λ' = 0,3,2,1 for λ = 0,1,2,3, as in the previous page's table.

checkable.sympy: all(l == -Mod(-l,4) + 4*(1 if l!=0 else 0) for l in range(4))
checkable.asserts: λ = −λ' + 4[λ≠0], the decomposition used for part IV (+4Σε over λ≠0, minus Σλ'ε).

transcription_corrections: In IV the struck word before 'gerade' is 'positiv' (crossed out), so the line reads '[X] gerade und nicht zugleich [x] gerade [y] gerade'.
In III the corrected condition is 'x eine Ganze, [y] Ungerade': 'X' is overwritten by 'x', and '[x] Gerade' is struck and replaced by '[y] Ungerade' below.
The definition of s appears to carry a sign stroke before 'Int.': likely 's = −Int.(½−ω)mi', consistent with the negative s entries in the next page's table.
In V, 'x eine Ganze' is written with x overwritten (possibly X → x), mirroring the correction in III.
